examples-typography.msg0001: Explore Liberation web fonts, 24 language samples, real subset loading and copyable typography recipes.
examples-typography.msg0014: One family of ideas.<s0></s0>Many ways to read.
examples-typography.msg0015: Liberation gives our laboratories a consistent voice across interfaces, texts, code and languages. This site uses the actual WOFF2 files prepared by Philipp Klinz in LiberationFontsWeb, served locally with each laboratory.
examples-typography.msg0021: Choose a family for the job. Regular, italic, bold and bold italic are real faces at weights 400 and 700.
examples-typography.msg0022: Interfaces, navigation and everyday reading. This is the default voice of the laboratory.
examples-typography.msg0023: Editorial emphasis, quotations and longer reading. Give paragraphs comfortable line spacing.
examples-typography.msg0024: Code, identifiers and aligned numbers. Equal character widths make sequences easier to compare.
examples-typography.msg0025: Compact headings and short labels. Keep reading text comfortably sized instead of squeezing more into every line.
examples-typography.msg0026: Try the writing you actually use.
examples-typography.msg0027: Change the family, face or sample language, then edit the text. Changing the interface language preserves your experiment.
examples-typography.msg0037: The sample stays on this page. Nothing you type is sent to a server.
examples-typography.msg0039: Choose a Greek or Bulgarian sample, or try the mathematical symbols. The monitor reads the preview's own font faces without preloading them.
examples-typography.msg0044: Already loaded faces stay available while you explore. File sizes describe the stored WOFF2 files, not network traffic: the browser may reuse its cache.
examples-typography.msg0046: The browser matches family, weight, style and characters. A language can use several subsets; different languages can share one. The lang attribute describes the language, while unicode-range controls character matching.
examples-typography.msg0048: font-display: swap lets fallback text appear while the requested font becomes available. It controls display timing; it does not choose the subset.
examples-typography.msg0050: These files cover Latin, extended Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and selected mathematical symbols. Combining marks, emoji and other scripts may use fallback fonts. The math subset is not a complete equation font.
examples-typography.msg0051: Use the same files in your laboratory.
examples-typography.msg0052: The starter already includes the fonts. Keep its fonts folder beside modern-objectivity.css when copying it. No CDN, package runtime or build step is needed.
examples-typography.msg0054: For a separate project, copy the font folder with its notices and load the bundle. You can also choose an individual family stylesheet.
examples-typography.msg0056: Use the Web family names. Keep generic fallbacks for unavailable fonts or characters. Request 400 or 700 when you want the supplied regular or bold face.
examples-typography.msg0058: This is the regular Greek face from the package. Declaring it makes it available; using matching characters causes the browser to request it. Avoid preloading every subset.
examples-typography.msg0060: Use the correct lang value for pronunciation, hyphenation and language-aware tools. Selecting a font does not translate content or guarantee that every glyph is present.
examples-typography.msg0062: The font files are copied unchanged from Philipp Klinz's LiberationFontsWeb repository. The package records its source commit and file hashes. Sans, Serif and Mono retain the SIL Open Font License; Sans Narrow's upstream GPL license and font exception are also included.

examples-accessibility.msg0004: Make every action reachable, understandable and recoverable.
examples-accessibility.msg0005: WCAG 2.2 AA is the target. These examples and checks are a starting point, not a conformance certificate.
examples-accessibility.msg0008: Use Tab and Shift + Tab to move, Enter or Space to activate buttons, and Escape to close the dialog.
examples-accessibility.msg0010: Open the dialog with the keyboard. Focus enters it and returns to this button when you close it.
examples-accessibility.msg0013: The background is inactive while this dialog is open. Tab stays inside; Escape closes it.
examples-accessibility.msg0017: Buttons, links and form controls already have keyboard behaviour. Keep a visible focus indicator and a logical reading order.
examples-accessibility.msg0019: Submit the empty form, then correct it. The error names the problem; your input stays intact.
examples-accessibility.msg0021: Use at least two characters. This form is a local exercise.
examples-accessibility.msg0024: A label, an associated error and an announced result make the form understandable without relying on colour.
examples-accessibility.msg0026: The system preference always wins. The checkbox can reduce movement further.
examples-accessibility.msg0030: People may read, listen, enlarge or navigate by headings. The same information must remain available.
examples-accessibility.msg0032: Describe an image’s purpose. Decorative images need empty alternative text; charts need a useful summary and accessible data.
examples-accessibility.msg0035: Provide captions and transcripts. Describe meaningful visual information that is missing from the audio.
examples-accessibility.msg0038: Use headings, landmarks, table headers and explicit labels. Declare the page language and mark language changes.
examples-accessibility.msg0041: Check complete tasks, including errors and dialogs. Test with assistive technology and involve people with disabilities.
examples-accessibility.msg0043: Every action works by keyboard, with visible focus and no keyboard trap.
examples-accessibility.msg0044: Text and controls remain usable at 200% text size and at 400% zoom; check reflow at 320 CSS pixels.
examples-accessibility.msg0045: Normal text reaches 4.5:1 contrast; large text and essential control graphics reach 3:1. Colour is not the only cue.
examples-accessibility.msg0046: Labels, errors, names, roles and state changes are understandable with a screen reader.
examples-accessibility.msg0047: Pointer targets meet the 24 CSS pixel minimum or its exceptions. This kit aims for 44 pixel buttons.
examples-accessibility.msg0048: Images, charts and media have useful alternatives. Reading order and headings make sense.
examples-accessibility.msg0049: Reduced motion is respected. Ongoing movement can be paused; content does not flash.
examples-accessibility.msg0050: Test results record the pages, states, browsers and assistive technology used, plus remaining limitations.
examples-accessibility.msg0052: Automated checks find only some barriers. A clean scan does not establish WCAG conformance.

contributing.msg0001: Contributing to Modern Objectivity / Modern Objectivity
contributing.msg0005: Contributions should make the language clearer, more applicable, technically grounded, and easier to verify.
contributing.msg0007: Explain <s0>problem → rationale → proposal → alternatives → verification → limitations</s0>. Design rules should name their scope. Provide illustrative examples or documented evidence; never imply a hypothetical test has been performed.
contributing.msg0009: Maintain <s0>English as the authoring source</s0> for this repository. Publish the complete style guide, handbook, examples and reader-facing contributor guidance in all 24 official EU languages.
contributing.msg0010: Write so a new reader can understand the guidance without external context.
contributing.msg0011: Exclude company identities, confidential applications, private project notes, or chat references.
contributing.msg0012: Distinguish a design language from a brand, UI theme, component library, and software framework.
contributing.msg0013: Avoid invented performance benchmarks, accessibility certifications, universal emotion claims, or unsupported superiority claims.
contributing.msg0014: Consider technical feasibility, accessibility, ethics, and subjective human experience.
contributing.msg0015: Respect copyright and attribution for external research, text, and imagery.
contributing.msg0016: Update cross-links, examples, and templates when changing a principle.
contributing.msg0017: Apply <s0>MO-13</s0> to the whole published guide as well as adopting applications. Published technical documentation is part of that coverage; English source files are an authoring choice, not a publication exemption.
contributing.msg0019: Edit the English Markdown or keyed source messages first, then reconcile the affected translations and regenerate published pages. Keep headings, link labels, tables, image descriptions and explanatory prose within the translation inventory. Preserve executable code, API identifiers, original bibliographic titles and the authoritative GPL text; translate the surrounding explanations.
contributing.msg0020: Before release, check all published pages and examples against the complete 24-language inventory, source revisions, placeholders and navigation. Check dynamic feedback and accessible names as well as initial text. Record these mechanical checks separately from linguistic review: the current translations are AI-assisted and await independent language review. Do not mark a translation current merely to silence a failing check.
contributing.msg0021: Preserve principle IDs where possible. If a definition changes materially, document compatibility implications.

docs-01-introduction.msg0005: Modern Objectivity is a design language for digital systems, scientific applications, interactive laboratories, and information-rich interfaces. It is independent of any organization, product, framework, or visual brand.
docs-01-introduction.msg0007: <s0>Design and engineering silos:</s0> a visually polished mockup is not a functioning, tested interface. Technical correctness alone also does not guarantee usability.
docs-01-introduction.msg0008: <s0>Inconsistent applications:</s0> separately authored modules often reinvent navigation, filtering, feedback, and input behavior, forcing users to relearn familiar tasks.
docs-01-introduction.msg0009: <s0>Duplicated components:</s0> unnecessary one-off solutions increase maintenance effort and introduce inconsistent behavior.
docs-01-introduction.msg0010: <s0>Unexamined imitation:</s0> a ready-made theme or visual convention may not suit a project's purpose.
docs-01-introduction.msg0011: <s0>Complex information:</s0> data, uncertainty, relationships, provenance, and time require deliberate representation.
docs-01-introduction.msg0012: <s0>Unvalidated claims:</s0> “intuitive”, “clear”, and “fast” should be tested rather than asserted.
docs-01-introduction.msg0014: A design language describes principles and reasoning. A design system turns selected decisions into tokens, components, and patterns. Implemented products must demonstrate real behavior.
docs-01-introduction.msg0015: <s0>Problem → requirement → design hypothesis → functional prototype → observation → revision.</s0>
docs-01-introduction.msg0017: Improve orientation, interpretability, reuse, robustness, accessibility, design independence, human experience, and accountability. These are goals, not automatic outcomes. Define success criteria locally.
docs-01-introduction.msg0019: The principles apply broadly. Shared behavioral conventions apply within a specific platform. Each project defines a distinct visual <s0>stage</s0>. Modern Objectivity does <s1>not</s1> impose one palette, typeface, layout, or logo on all adopters.
docs-01-introduction.msg0020: Do not confuse aesthetic preference with a claim of empirical evidence. A project may intentionally pursue beauty or fascination, but must name that intention honestly.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0006: Modern Objectivity is not an instruction to make interfaces visually cold or minimalist. It is a method: observe, question, reason, prototype, test, explain, improve. Design contains subjective and aesthetic choices; the method requires those choices to be distinguished from factual or measured claims.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0008: <s0>Point:</s0> an identifiable element, measurement, entity, position, event, or observation.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0009: <s0>Line:</s0> a relation, direction, boundary, link, development, or connection.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0010: <s0>Space:</s0> the organization of elements and their relationships, whether flat, layered, or spatial.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0011: <s0>Time:</s0> durations, transitions, system states, history, update frequency, and information freshness.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0012: These are conceptual elements, not mandatory geometric graphics. Three-dimensional displays are not inherently superior to tables or two-dimensional diagrams.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0014: A <s0>stage</s0> is the consistent designed environment in which interaction takes place. It possesses its own identity and may be restrained or expressive. A <s1>set</s1> is the content-specific arrangement, such as a data view, experiment, scientific visualization, or artwork. A <s2>performance</s2> is the actual behavior of stage and content over time.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0015: A shared language can lead to very different stages. However, equivalent interactions within one application should remain consistent.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0017: Human experience is not outside the design problem. <s0>Emotional Intent</s0> means a deliberately planned experience, such as calm during administrative work, curiosity during learning, or fascination during exploration. <s1>Subjective Experience</s1> is the actual experience of a person in context. The first influences design; the second can be observed and reported, then used to revise the design.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0018: Emotional goals are therefore both design inputs and potential outcomes. They are not guaranteed, and human experience is not simply an additional geometric primitive.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0020: Do not suggest technical reliability that is absent, portray uncertainty as certainty, or use misleading urgency and hidden consequences. Emotional effectiveness must not depend on manipulation.
docs-02-philosophy.msg0022: Historical movements may inspire comparative questions about technology, form, and function, but do not provide the authority or required appearance of this language.
docs-03-principles.msg0005: The following principles guide implementation and review. Apply them to actual tasks and verify their implementation with appropriate evidence. MO-13 defines the required language-coverage baseline; partial implementation must be identified explicitly.
docs-03-principles.msg0010: <s0>Purpose before appearance.</s0> State the functional or expressive aim of a decision.
docs-03-principles.msg0013: <s0>Honest representation.</s0> Preserve the meaning of data, uncertainty, status, and relationships.
docs-03-principles.msg0014: Can users correctly interpret the information?
docs-03-principles.msg0016: <s0>Consistency of equivalent behavior.</s0> Similar actions within one environment should behave similarly.
docs-03-principles.msg0019: <s0>Controlled diversity.</s0> Define invariants, variables, and expressive freedoms.
docs-03-principles.msg0022: <s0>Reuse before reinvention.</s0> Examine tested components before writing new equivalents.
docs-03-principles.msg0025: <s0>Design time and states.</s0> Consider waiting, success, errors, partial data, and recovery.
docs-03-principles.msg0026: What happens before, during, and after an action?
docs-03-principles.msg0028: <s0>Engineering is part of design.</s0> Evaluate feasibility with real operating constraints.
docs-03-principles.msg0029: Can the proposal function with realistic conditions?
docs-03-principles.msg0031: <s0>Accessibility is foundational.</s0> Provide usable navigation, input, and perception paths.
docs-03-principles.msg0034: <s0>Structure complexity without hiding it.</s0> Keep essential detail discoverable.
docs-03-principles.msg0035: Can users move from overview to detail?
docs-03-principles.msg0037: <s0>Validate design claims.</s0> Test hypotheses and document what was actually observed.
docs-03-principles.msg0040: <s0>Make systems explainable.</s0> Communicate state, causes, and consequences.
docs-03-principles.msg0041: Can someone tell what the system does and why?
docs-03-principles.msg0043: <s0>Emotion as Function.</s0> Consider emotional and aesthetic effects as legitimate goals, not assured results.
docs-03-principles.msg0044: Is the intended experience supported and ethically appropriate?
docs-03-principles.msg0046: <s0>Language is part of access.</s0> Provide complete user-facing journeys, including the published guide, handbook and examples, in all 24 official EU languages, with honest coverage status.
docs-03-principles.msg0047: Can people understand the content, operate the interface and receive feedback in their selected language?
docs-03-principles.msg0049: <s0>Honesty:</s0> Distinguish zero from missing, observations from predictions, and decorative charts from measured data.
docs-03-principles.msg0050: <s0>Consistency:</s0> A specialist module may have a unique diagram without inventing its own universal navigation or error behavior.
docs-03-principles.msg0051: <s0>Realism:</s0> A mockup cannot demonstrate keyboard handling, resilience to long identifiers, performance, or successful error recovery.
docs-03-principles.msg0052: <s0>Accessibility:</s0> Test keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic labels, magnification, and alternatives to pointer-only interactions.
docs-03-principles.msg0053: <s0>Language access:</s0> Design translations, plural forms, flexible layouts and state-preserving language changes from the start. Follow <s1>Multilingual Access</s1>, the central requirement, and the <s2>working programming pattern</s2>. A phased rollout must not be advertised as complete 24-language support.
docs-03-principles.msg0054: <s0>Validation:</s0> A design can be attractive and still fail its task; a successful task can still feel stressful. System performance, behavior, and subjective reports are different evidence sources.
docs-03-principles.msg0056: Record the purpose, options, tradeoffs, and evaluation in a design decision record. For example, a 3D scientific graph may support exploration but require a table for exact values or non-spatial access. Never trade away truthful reporting or required accessibility for decorative novelty.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0005: Modern Objectivity prescribes <s0>reasoned visual organization</s0>, not a universal style.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0007: Identify entities, relationships, tasks, actions, provenance, uncertainty, data age, and expected density before choosing aesthetics. A visually simple interface can still be difficult to understand.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0009: Use alignment, proximity, spacing, shape, and boundaries to reveal relationships. A grid is a construction tool, not an arbitrary constraint. Lines may indicate a boundary, relation, sequence, or deliberate visual rhythm; avoid accidental diagram-like decoration.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0011: Define roles for page and section headings, body text, labels, code, technical identifiers, numeric data, help, and statuses. Choose fonts based on the application's content and language requirements. Test long names, variable-length translations, symbols, and confusable characters.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0012: Use scale-aware sizing, readable line lengths, adequate spacing, and tabular figures where comparisons require aligned digits.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0014: Use <s0>semantic roles</s0>: surface, text, interactive accent, focus, status, category, quantitative scale, and expressive atmosphere. Map these to a project-specific palette. Important meaning must not depend on color alone.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0015: Material effects such as blur, shadows, glass, texture, and gradients may reinforce hierarchy or artistic expression but must not obscure content.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0016: There is no official Modern Objectivity color, font, icon family, or logo.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0018: Scientific tools may need compact density without sacrificing readability or input accessibility. Narrow screens may require alternate navigation rather than merely shrinking columns. Test real high-volume and edge-case content.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0020: Distinguish factual charts, explanatory diagrams, navigation graphics, and decorative imagery. Use units, legends, source information, and appropriate axes in factual charts. Never let an illustrative scale masquerade as a measurement.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0022: <s0>Primitives:</s0> raw values such as spacing and palette steps.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0024: <s0>Component tokens:</s0> purpose within a component such as <s1></s1>.
docs-04-visual-language.msg0026: Each token needs purpose, scope, variants, and maintenance ownership. Do not turn every one-off visual value into a global token.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0006: A meaningful action requires <s0>preconditions → input → acknowledgment → processing → outcome or failure → recovery</s0>. A click animation is not enough.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0025: Provide a way to revise filters
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0037: Do not disguise as missing records
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0041: Not every control needs every state. Specify the applicable subset explicitly.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0043: Report whether work has succeeded, failed, or has an unknown outcome. Never fabricate progress percentages. Support undo or recovery for high-impact actions where feasible. Dialogs should manage keyboard focus reliably.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0044: Within a system, keep selection, hover, keyboard focus, and active navigation distinguishable. Preserve the user's search/filter context when returning from a detail page if appropriate.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0046: Distinguish <s0>functional motion</s0> that clarifies transitions, <s1>data-driven motion</s1> that depicts changing values, and <s2>atmospheric motion</s2> that creates an experience. Each requires different evaluation. Provide reduced-motion alternatives and never hide critical meaning in brief animation.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0048: Time ranges, timestamps, update cadence, and freshness affect meaning. Mark live, cached, historical, simulated, and predicted data when applicable. Avoid automatic content reordering that disrupts reading.
docs-05-time-interaction.msg0050: Emotional Intent may evolve across a task: curiosity at entry, concentration during work, appropriate concern at real risks, and satisfaction after confirmed success. This is a planned hypothesis, not an emotional guarantee.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0006: A <s0>stage</s0> is a designed environment for a specific product or experiment. It has its own layout, typography, navigation, timing, and character. A quiet information interface and a visually immersive science exhibit can share Modern Objectivity without looking alike.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0007: The <s0>set</s0> is content and its contextual expression. The <s1>performance</s1> is the running experience, including interaction and time.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0014: Consistent behavior within a defined environment
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0022: A rule binding one host application does not automatically bind unrelated projects.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0024: A host can own navigation, basic controls, permission semantics, feedback, and shared component contracts. Modules provide domain content, specialized actions, and purpose-built visualizations.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0025: An extension may add a novel scientific chart while retaining established search and error behavior. Specialization should not force users to relearn universal interactions.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0027: Distinctiveness can arise from proportions, information architecture, typography, imagery, materials, and temporal behavior. Replacing familiar controls with unfamiliar ones merely to appear original is rarely useful.
docs-06-stage-identity.msg0029: Every stage should describe purpose, audience, invariants, variables, expression, accessibility alternatives, Emotional Intent, adverse effects, and validation method.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0006: Prototype complete interaction slices early. Test representative data, input, loading, failures, long strings, permissions, and scale. A visually polished image is not a working component.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0008: For applicable web projects, consider <s0>WCAG 2.2</s0> Level AA as a baseline; concrete legal requirements are context-specific. This handbook does not certify compliance.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0009: Prefer semantic native controls. Test keyboard navigation, focus visibility, labels, assistive technology, zoom and reflow, contrast, and alternatives to complex visual gestures. Automated checks are insufficient on their own.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0011: Set locally meaningful budgets for devices, latency, data volume, and memory. Do not assume universal performance numbers. Consider pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, reduced-complexity display, or degraded-mode operation when necessary.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0012: Test slow and missing responses, duplicate actions, changing permissions, and unknown outcomes.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0014: Implement <s0>MO-13: Multilingual Access</s0>: complete user-facing journeys in all 24 official EU languages, including the entire published guide, handbook and examples. Keep model values separate from keyed message catalogues, use locale-aware formatting and plural rules, and preserve application state when changing language. Test long text, Greek/Cyrillic glyphs, accessible descriptions and failure paths.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0015: The <s0>local-catalogue programming pattern</s0> supplies a working static example, source-revision checks and a copyable helper. It requires no remote translation service or cross-repository runtime. Coverage, source freshness and linguistic review are separate properties; report partial rollout honestly.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0017: A shared component specifies purpose, inputs, outputs, events, states, focus behavior, keyboard and screenreader behavior, semantic tokens, variants, errors, performance assumptions, tests, and versioning.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0020: Treat changes in status semantics, accessibility, component APIs, and design tokens as potentially breaking. Record the reason, scope, owner, migration strategy, and test results.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0021: A local rule can move through <s0>draft → evaluated → adopted → superseded</s0>.
docs-07-technical-principles.msg0023: Do not imply a security property from appearance alone. Show permission and failure states accurately, without exposing secrets in client-side messages or logs.
docs-08-validation.msg0006: Design is a hypothesis about function, interpretation, or experience. Use an iterative process:
docs-08-validation.msg0008: Set functional and, when relevant, emotional goals.
docs-08-validation.msg0009: Identify a falsifiable or otherwise examinable assumption.
docs-08-validation.msg0011: Select success criteria before collecting results.
docs-08-validation.msg0012: Observe behavior, system properties, and subjective reports.
docs-08-validation.msg0014: Adopt, narrow, change, or reject the design; repeat as needed.
docs-08-validation.msg0029: Complete journey coverage, source freshness, language-specific plurals/formatting, translated graphics and state-preserving switches
docs-08-validation.msg0045: <s0>E4:</s0> behavior observed in real use and assumptions revisited.
docs-08-validation.msg0046: These classify <s0>evidence type</s0>, not universal quality. Do not call an E1 mockup “tested”.
docs-08-validation.msg0048: For reusable components, test normal content; empty versus no results; errors and permission denial; long and large datasets; keyboard/focus; relevant locales; loading and retries; integration with the host.
docs-08-validation.msg0049: Document exceptions if a scenario is not applicable.
docs-08-validation.msg0050: For <s0>MO-13</s0>, inventory every published page, handbook chapter and example, then check each language for complete content, missing keys, stale source revisions, placeholder changes and plural forms. Check prose, tables, navigation, metadata and link destinations alongside controls, feedback, graphics and accessible descriptions. Test fallback, deep links, back/forward, long text and Greek/Cyrillic text. Automatic coverage checks do not establish linguistic or scientific correctness. Record translation review separately; keep unimplemented coverage visible.
docs-08-validation.msg0052: Define the desired experience, possible mechanism, adverse effects, and suitable investigation. Distinguish <s0>measured system properties</s0>, <s1>observed user behavior</s1>, and <s2>subjective reports</s2>. A quick task may still be stressful, and a compelling simulation may not teach the underlying principle.
docs-08-validation.msg0054: <s0>Research console:</s0> Can participants transfer search and detail navigation knowledge between independently authored modules?
docs-08-validation.msg0055: <s0>Learning simulation:</s0> Does visible cause-and-effect support exploration and correct conceptual understanding? Do reported feelings match the intended curiosity?
docs-08-validation.msg0056: <s0>Sensor dashboard:</s0> Can participants identify freshness, missing values, units, and uncertainty?
docs-08-validation.msg0057: These are test designs, <s0>not completed studies</s0>.
docs-08-validation.msg0058: Use the <s0>Validation Plan</s0> and <s1>Design Decision Record</s1>.
docs-09-references.msg0005: References provide comparisons and historical orientation. They do not serve as authority for a design rule.
docs-09-references.msg0007: Bauhaus, Neue Sachlichkeit, constructivist approaches, and international typographic traditions explored form, function, technology, and communication. Their appearance is not a required visual specification for Modern Objectivity.
docs-09-references.msg0014: These already address complex interactions, accessibility, components, and motion. Modern Objectivity does not claim uniqueness for those features.
docs-09-references.msg0016: Define comparison criteria such as modular integration, temporal data, consistency, theme flexibility, validation, accessibility, and component governance. Avoid unsupported superiority claims.
docs-09-references.msg0017: Attribute research and respect rights in borrowed text, figures, diagrams, and code.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0005: <s0>MO-13: language is part of access.</s0> Applications adopting Modern Objectivity must provide complete user-facing journeys in all <s1>24 official EU languages</s1>. The same requirement applies to the entire published Modern Objectivity style guide, handbook, technical guidance and every example. Additional languages are welcome.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0006: Implementations may expand coverage incrementally, but must report partial coverage honestly. A language selector, translated navigation or a list of planned languages does not establish a translated application.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0007: This document is the central requirement. The <s0>programming pattern</s0> supplies a practical static implementation; application repositories own their content, release schedule and local copies. They must not depend on this website at runtime.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0009: Use language tags and native names. Flags identify countries, not languages. A language tag need not dictate a single regional format: state any chosen regional conventions explicitly.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0059: The <s0>copyable language registry</s0> implements these tags. The example uses <s1></s1> and <s2></s2> for English and Portuguese number/plural formatting; its content tags remain <s3></s3> and <s4></s4>.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0061: Complete journeys include navigation, teaching content, controls, input help, validation, loading/empty/error states, exercise questions and answers, feedback, search vocabulary, glossary definitions and recovery paths. Include text inside charts, SVG, Canvas and 3D views, and accessible equivalents such as labels, descriptions and announcements. Translate headings, paragraphs, tables, link labels, image descriptions, document titles and metadata throughout the published guide and handbook.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0062: Preserve scientific meaning: evidence, uncertainty, dates, signs, units, model limitations and answer correctness. Equations, executable source code, API identifiers, sequences, raw data and taxonomic names are shared; translate their explanations and all user-facing text rendered by examples. Original bibliographic titles and attributed quotations may remain in their original language with an appropriate language indication. Preserve the authoritative GPL license text; translate surrounding licensing guidance without presenting it as a replacement legal text. External source documents need not be translated. Personal notes remain as authored.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0063: English Markdown remains this repository's authoring source. Its published handbook editions must carry the complete content in all 24 languages, including contributor and implementation guidance. Technical subject matter and an embedded translated component do not exempt the surrounding page from coverage. Set the page language to the language actually displayed, and identify preserved foreign-language passages separately.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0065: Make language choice visible and keyboard-accessible. Use native names, a real control label and a stable shareable URL. Preserve the language across supported chapter links and return paths.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0066: Language switching updates the presentation of the current state. Preserve inputs, selections, results, notes and progress; do not restart a model or generate new random data to translate its output.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0067: Translate whole messages with named placeholders. Support the language's plural categories and number/date conventions; do not concatenate translated sentence fragments or format data by replacing punctuation.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0068: Set <s0></s0> on the actual document or component and on foreign-language passages where needed. Update accessible descriptions together with visible labels.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0069: Allow text to wrap and controls to grow. Verify long translations, diacritics, Greek and Cyrillic glyphs, keyboard operation, zoom and narrow layouts. Do not solve overflow by hiding meaningful text.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0070: Keep translations available under the application's existing open-source/content licensing. Static labs retain <s0>STATIC BY DESIGN · OPEN ACCESS · OPEN SOURCE · NO ACCOUNTS · NO TRACKING</s0>. Language selection requires no account, telemetry or remote translation service.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0072: Maintain one application/model implementation with separate, local message catalogues. Use stable semantic keys, an explicit source language per module, a terminology glossary and source-version information. Reuse the coding convention without creating a mandatory cross-repository runtime. Local copies should record their upstream revision and can evolve independently.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0073: The source language is an editorial choice: an existing German lab can retain German, while this guide uses English. Translate against that source and its shared data; avoid untracked chains of translation through other languages. Source-language authoring does not narrow the published language baseline.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0074: Treat each lesson/module and its shared controls as a publication unit. Keep coverage (<s0></s0>, <s1></s1>, <s2></s2>) separate from source freshness and review provenance. The runtime must not advertise a draft, incomplete or stale pack as a complete language edition. A full lab is available in a language only when its entry page, every included module and shared controls are available and current.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0075: For a missing or invalid pack, keep a usable source-language module and clearly identify the fallback in the language actually displayed. Never silently label source-language content as the requested language. A failed switch must preserve the user's state.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0077: Author or revise a message in the module's source catalogue, or edit the English Markdown for handbook content. Keep context and terminology close to the text; do not duplicate model data in translated files.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0078: Use version-control diffs to translate only affected messages. A module-level source fingerprint identifies stale packs; large modules can later use per-key fingerprints without changing the user-facing contract.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0079: Check the complete published page inventory, key coverage, placeholders, plural forms and source freshness automatically across all 24 languages. Include handbook content, navigation, dynamic feedback and accessible text. Review semantic equivalence and rendering separately. A complete key count cannot establish linguistic or scientific accuracy.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0080: Update a translation's source revision only after reconciling the changed text. Do not mass-update revision fields to silence a failed check. Changes to model assumptions also require checking associated explanations.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0081: Record AI assistance and independent review accurately. AI-assisted publication is possible; do not imply professional, native-speaker or specialist verification that has not occurred. No paid translation service is required.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0083: The <s0>working sample</s0> demonstrates local message catalogues, plurals, formatting, source fallback and state-preserving language changes. Its small sampling module remains a copyable programming example; the containing page, the rest of the style kit and the complete handbook follow the same 24-language publication requirement.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0084: The showcase, console, experiment, dashboard starter, multilingual pattern and handbook belong to one publication scope. Coverage must be checked across all of them before claiming a complete edition. Translations are AI-assisted and await independent language review; mechanical checks establish coverage and source consistency, not professional linguistic verification or scientific validation.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0085: State each delivery choice explicitly: a page may use local JavaScript catalogues or generated static language editions. A source-language fallback must be labeled as such and must not be counted as a translated edition. If a project requires localized no-JavaScript documents or independently indexed language pages, generate those from the same maintained content. Runtime dependencies and offline limitations must remain visible.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0087: <s0>European Union: Languages</s0>, official list checked 24 November 2026.
docs-10-multilingual-access.msg0090: This is Modern Objectivity's own design requirement; it is not a claim that EU language policy legally obliges every application to implement these languages.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0001: Example — Interactive Learning Laboratory / Modern Objectivity
examples-interactive-learning.msg0005: <s0>Illustrative design scenario; not a report of empirical findings.</s0>
examples-interactive-learning.msg0006: A browser laboratory lets visitors change parameters and observe the effects on a scientific model.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0007: <s0>Functional intent:</s0> support cause-and-effect understanding, comparison, and accurate interpretation of model assumptions.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0008: <s0>Emotional Intent:</s0> encourage curiosity and exploration without requiring excitement to complete the learning task.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0009: <s0>Stage:</s0> understandable controls, reversible experiments, explicit source information, and accessible navigation.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0010: <s0>Set:</s0> an expressive dynamic model or visualization that responds to input.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0011: <s0>Risk:</s0> movement may obscure precise values or trigger discomfort. Visual fascination is not evidence of learning. A simplified simulation must not be mistaken for a full scientific measurement.
examples-interactive-learning.msg0012: <s0>Evaluation:</s0> ask learners to describe what changed, distinguish input from output, compare trials, and identify assumptions. Separately observe exploratory actions and collect subjective reports.
examples-modular-research-console.msg000: Example — Modular Research Console / Modern Objectivity
<s0>Illustrative design scenario; no user study has been completed for this example.</s0>

A shared research application hosts independently authored modules for instruments, datasets, and experiment results. Each has different domain content but relies on common navigation, search, selection, and feedback.
<s0>Hypothesis:</s0> people transfer learned list/detail workflows more readily between modules using the same conventions.
<s0>Host invariants:</s0> navigation, search semantics, state feedback, permission display, focus behavior.
<s0>Module freedoms:</s0> domain-specific data, specialist visualizations, contextual actions and explanatory diagrams.
examples-modular-research-console.msg001: <s0>Prototype:</s0> implement two distinct modules using one list/detail component contract. Include long identifiers, missing fields, slow requests, network errors, and permission denial.

<s0>Evaluation plan:</s0> ask participants to locate records, open detail views, return without losing filters, and recover after failure. Observe actions and ask about subjective clarity. Define criteria before the test.
<s0>Decision:</s0> if the shared pattern creates a domain-specific obstacle, revise its contract or record a justified exception.
guides-adoption.msg0005: Modern Objectivity is a design language, not a prebuilt UI theme. Adoption starts with the real task.
guides-adoption.msg0006: <s0>Inventory:</s0> identify users, contexts, tasks, content, states, data relationships, constraints, and recurring failures.
guides-adoption.msg0007: <s0>Stage:</s0> define a <s1>Stage Profile</s1>, separating invariants, variables, and expressive freedoms.
guides-adoption.msg0008: <s0>Principles:</s0> review the <s1>principles</s1>, including the required <s2>24-language access baseline</s2>, and record implementation gaps explicitly.
guides-adoption.msg0009: <s0>Prototype:</s0> build one meaningful working journey with realistic data, errors, navigation, and accessible interaction.
guides-adoption.msg0010: <s0>Validation:</s0> create a <s1>Validation Plan</s1>; decide what would count as success before testing.
guides-adoption.msg0011: <s0>Reuse:</s0> develop component contracts for repeated interaction patterns.
guides-adoption.msg0012: <s0>Govern:</s0> preserve rationale, versioning, results, and the decisions made.
guides-adoption.msg0014: Problem, context, and intended tasks are documented.
guides-adoption.msg0015: Stage-level navigation and semantics are explicit.
guides-adoption.msg0016: The visual identity is locally specified, rather than inherited by default.
guides-adoption.msg0017: Loading, empty, no-results, and failure states are addressed.
guides-adoption.msg0018: Data presentations are accurate and explainable.
guides-adoption.msg0019: Core tasks are accessible by supported input methods.
guides-adoption.msg0020: The 24-language baseline covers the complete published guidance, handbook, examples, interactions and accessible feedback; partial coverage is identified, with a migration path.
guides-adoption.msg0021: Message catalogues, source freshness and language review follow the
guides-adoption.msg0024: Emotional Intent, where relevant, is stated without promising a guaranteed effect.
guides-adoption.msg0025: Critical claims are accompanied by observations or a declared test plan.
guides-components.msg0005: A reusable component is a contract for behavior <s0>and</s0> presentation, not a screenshot.
guides-components.msg0007: Make current filters legible and revisable.
guides-components.msg0008: Distinguish an empty dataset from zero matching results.
guides-components.msg0009: Avoid presenting unknown totals as exact counts.
guides-components.msg0011: Keep keyboard focus and selection distinct.
guides-components.msg0012: Preserve relevant filter and navigation context when returning from a detail.
guides-components.msg0013: Test long labels, missing fields, and high-volume collections.
guides-components.msg0015: Provide persistent labels and actionable validation messages.
guides-components.msg0016: Explain whether changes are pending, saved, or rejected.
guides-components.msg0018: Provide recovery for destructive actions where feasible.
guides-components.msg0020: Use modal interruption only when necessary.
guides-components.msg0022: Describe consequences, not merely “Are you sure?”
guides-components.msg0024: Specify initial, loading, ready, empty, no-results, partial, stale, error, forbidden, and disabled only where relevant. A spinner alone cannot explain a failed operation.
guides-data-visualization.msg0005: A visualization begins with a question, not a chart style.
guides-data-visualization.msg0007: <s0>Temporal change:</s0> a time series or annotated timeline.
guides-data-visualization.msg0008: <s0>Exact values:</s0> a table or directly labeled representation.
guides-data-visualization.msg0011: <s0>Position:</s0> a map or other coordinate-based representation.
guides-data-visualization.msg0013: Identify quantities, units, time windows, and meaningful baselines.
guides-data-visualization.msg0014: Separate missing, zero, unknown, and not applicable.
guides-data-visualization.msg0015: Label measurements, simulations, and predictions distinctly.
guides-data-visualization.msg0016: Explain transformations, aggregation, normalization, and uncertainty.
guides-data-visualization.msg0017: Show provenance and freshness when interpretation depends on them.
guides-data-visualization.msg0018: Avoid color-only distinctions; provide legends and accessible value alternatives.
guides-data-visualization.msg0019: Never use decoration that looks like measured data without clearly distinguishing it.
guides-data-visualization.msg0021: Support useful overview-to-detail navigation. Do not let animated transitions hide factual values. Avoid automatic refreshing that disrupts focus or reading.
guides-data-visualization.msg0023: <s0>Bad:</s0> a sensor line connects across three missing readings, implying continuous observation.
guides-data-visualization.msg0024: <s0>Better:</s0> mark the gap, show the sampling interval and latest valid measurement, and expose a table of original values.
guides-data-visualization.msg0026: Can a reader correctly tell what was measured, when, how uncertain it is, and what was not observed?
guides-emotional-intent.msg0005: Emotion can be an intentionally designed function rather than a decorative afterthought.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0007: <s0>Emotional Intent</s0> is the experience the designer hopes to support. <s1>Subjective Experience</s1> is what a person actually feels or reports within their context. A design cannot guarantee a particular emotional reaction.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0010: Name the desired experience: e.g., calm, curiosity, fascination, or appropriate concern.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0012: Consider unintended effects on different people.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0013: Preserve usable alternatives if the emotional intent is not achieved.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0014: Evaluate both behavior and subjective reports.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0016: <s0>Research console:</s0> stable navigation and precise feedback can support calm and control; an overly quiet warning can conceal genuine risk.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0017: <s0>Learning experiment:</s0> responsive simulations can foster curiosity; enjoyment alone does not establish understanding.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0018: <s0>Spatial exhibition:</s0> motion and layered imagery can support wonder; provide reduced-motion and non-spatial access.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0020: An experience may move from curiosity during exploration, to focus during a task, to concern at a genuine warning, to satisfaction after a confirmed result. This is a testable design hypothesis, not a mandatory script.
guides-emotional-intent.msg0022: Distinguish system properties, observed behavior, and subjective reports. Avoid fabricated urgency, false reassurance, covert manipulation, and user-blaming interpretations of different emotional responses.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0001: Programming Pattern — Local Catalogues, Shared State / Modern Objectivity
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0004: Programming Pattern — Local Catalogues, Shared State
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0005: <s0>Open the working example</s0> · <s1>Copyable files</s1> · <s2>Central requirement: MO-13</s2>
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0006: Keep three responsibilities separate: <s0>model values</s0>, <s1>translated messages</s1>, and <s2>rendering</s2>. Language changes re-render the current values. They never replace the model with a language-specific copy.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0008: The sampling model uses 13 message keys; each local catalogue also covers the surrounding page. Its source language is English; an existing lab may instead choose German. A catalogue is data wrapped in a classic script, allowing direct-file loading as well as static hosting without a JSON fetch or a build step.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0010: Polish supplies its own forms under the same key:
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0011: Stable keys describe meaning, not current wording or a DOM position. Keep model constants, answer IDs and scientific datasets outside catalogues. Split a large lab into shared controls plus individual module catalogues; namespace keys before combining them, check both source revisions and load only those needed by the current page. The supplied example is intentionally one small module, not a general catalogue framework.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0013: <s0></s0> translates explicitly marked text leaves and the supported <s1></s1>, <s2></s2> and <s3></s3> bindings. It sets the scope's language. For a complete page, the scope can be <s4></s4>, with a bound <s5></s5>; update metadata explicitly. A module may use a narrower scope, but its containing page still needs complete translated content under MO-13. Numeric feedback and the SVG description are rendered explicitly using the same helper.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0014: Messages are inserted with <s0></s0> or named attributes. The helper does not interpret translated HTML. Use semantic DOM slots for rich paragraphs, links and emphasis when adding them; preserve reorderable full messages instead of assembling sentences from fragments. Do not mark containers containing live controls as replaceable text.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0016: <s0></s0> only accepts exact tags from <s1></s1>, loads the selected local script once, and checks the catalogue before selecting it. An incomplete, stale or draft catalogue causes a whole-module source fallback with a visible notice. Unknown tags cannot become arbitrary script paths. Late responses from an earlier selection cannot override the latest choice; a failed request can be retried.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0017: The URL uses <s0></s0>. Explicit switches preserve other query parameters and hashes, and browser back/forward restores the language. A share link exposes the active language. No browser-language redirect, account, cookie or preference storage is involved. Existing language-less links remain valid. Other projects can choose their own URL convention if the same navigation contract is preserved.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0018: The example's source pack is loaded first, so its readable English HTML remains the baseline. If JavaScript is disabled, initial source values are shown and interactive controls are disabled. For downloaded copies, classic scripts avoid the local-file restrictions associated with fetching JSON. Some browsers restrict History changes on <s0></s0>; the share link still carries the language.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0020: Each pack records <s0></s0>, <s1></s1> and <s2></s2>. In the example, status is <s3></s3>; a production module uses <s4></s4> only after the appropriate content and interaction checks. Planned/draft editions must not be listed as completed choices in a production selector.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0021: The check hashes the canonical source messages and compares every pack against that fingerprint. It checks keys, placeholders and all plural categories for the chosen locale. Editing source text makes unreconciled translations fail. To print the new fingerprint without changing any files:
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0022: Review the source diff, update the affected translated messages, then record that fingerprint in each reconciled pack. Update the source pack's fingerprint too. Do not recopy or retranslate unchanged messages. This module-level approach intentionally favors a small, inspectable mechanism; per-key revision metadata can be introduced if a larger editorial workload justifies it.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0023: Apply the same maintenance rule to the complete published guide. English Markdown is the authoring source for the HTML handbook pages. After a source edit, reconcile affected translated prose, headings, tables and link labels, regenerate the published pages and check all 24 language editions. Keep code and API identifiers stable while translating their explanations. Navigation between the guide, handbook and examples must retain the selected language. These mechanical checks are separate from independent linguistic review, which remains pending for the AI-assisted translations.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0024: The browser check covers all 24 choices at several widths, state preservation, plural output, accessible SVG text, URL navigation, failed loads, source fallback, rapid selection and direct-file use. Run it with a development-only Playwright installation as documented in the <s0>pattern README</s0>. Neither Node nor Playwright is shipped as a runtime dependency.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0026: The helper covers plain messages, cardinal plurals, named parameters and number formatting. It is not an ICU MessageFormat engine, automatic translator, rich-text CMS, localized search engine or lesson renderer. Long-form lessons, localized search indexes and Canvas/Three.js labels need explicit integration using the same keys and shared-state contract. It provides no independent guarantee of translation quality, scientific correctness or accessibility compliance.
guides-multilingual-pattern.msg0027: If richer grammar or nested messages warrant an established formatter later, vendor and document it locally. Preserve the language-access contract rather than treating this small implementation as mandatory for every application.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0001: Visual Style Specification — Reference Lab Theme v0.1 / Modern Objectivity
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0004: Visual Style Specification — Reference Lab Theme v0.1
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0005: This page documents the <s0>actual CSS implementation</s0>, not theoretical recommendations. The <s1>style showcase</s1> and working laboratories use <s2>the same source stylesheet</s2>. The <s3>starter</s3> and <s4>multilingual pattern</s4> include standalone copies.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0007: <s0>Character:</s0> structured laboratory instrument / editorial technical interface.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0008: <s0>Composition:</s0> deep graphite navigation rail, precise typography, restrained low-relief cards, thin lines, high information density with generous reading space.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0009: <s0>Default:</s0> light canvas with teal action accent; dark mode supported through semantic tokens.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0010: <s0>Type:</s0> Locally served Liberation Sans Web for UI and reading, Liberation Mono Web for technical labels and figures, Liberation Serif Web for editorial accents; system fallbacks remain available.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0011: <s0>Layout:</s0> 4 px base rhythm, square corners (0 px radius) on all UI containers and controls, clear type hierarchy.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0012: <s0>Interaction:</s0> visible focus, semantic status distinctions, filterable data, explicit handling of empty/error states.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0013: This is the first <s0>practical example skin</s0>, not a restriction that every adopting project must use the same colors.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0018: For all values, including status colors, consult the CSS. Recheck contrast before changing tokens.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0058: <s0>Explore families, languages and subset loading in the typography lab</s0>.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0020: The full shell uses a 254 px navigation rail and fluid content area. At 900 px width or narrower, navigation becomes a horizontal, scrollable section. At 640 px or narrower, content grids become single-column. Data tables maintain readable columns and scroll horizontally rather than compressing values beyond recognition.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0040: Use ARIA tab and panel semantics
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0044: A lab should implement a meaningful handler for its actions. Styling alone does not create behavior.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0045: 6. Change the style for your own lab
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0046: Override semantic roles rather than replacing each component selector:
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0047: Check contrast, focus visibility and status differentiation again after any palette changes.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0049: <s0>Style showcase</s0>: theme switching, active tabs, input controls, filterable table, simulated progress and toast feedback.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0050: <s0>Lab console</s0>: local synthetic data generation, status classification, filtering, detail inspection, chart updates and CSV export.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0051: <s0>Live experiment</s0>: mathematically defined wave, changing parameters, pause, play, step, reset and inspectable probe values.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0052: <s0>Standalone starter</s0>: working application shell, local synthetic observations, search, filtering, CSV export and clear empty state.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0053: <s0>Multilingual pattern</s0>: a 24-language sample panel with local catalogues, number/plural formatting, state-preserving switches and source checks. <s1>MO-13</s1> applies to the entire published style kit, all examples and handbook content.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0054: <s0>Data integrity:</s0> Every generated value is explicitly labeled synthetic. No example implies a real instrument has been connected or a user study has been completed.
guides-visual-style-spec.msg0056: The stylesheet is a concrete starting point; it does not certify WCAG compliance or universal usability. Verify it on target browsers, devices and assistive technologies before deploying a production laboratory. No backend, authentication, storage or external instrumentation is provided.
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0006: Copy this entire folder into an independent project. Open <s0></s0> directly, or serve it from any static server. No package manager, account or build step is required to use the page.

The surrounding page, handbook and other style-kit examples also belong to the complete 24-language publication scope; the panel's catalogue alone cannot establish site-wide coverage. Translations are AI-assisted and await independent language review. The arithmetic is an illustrative time budget, not a measurement or a physically validated simulation.
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0020: Node and Python are convenient authoring/checking tools, not requirements of the published site. For optional browser checks, install the test runner in your development checkout:
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0021: The browser check starts and stops its own local server. <s0></s0> can select an installed Chromium binary. Set <s1></s1> to save representative screenshots. The repository CI runs the same checks. No dependency files need to be deployed with the static page.
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0023: Choose the module's source language, replace the sample messages and model, and update the HTML source fallback. Add translated leaf text and accessible attributes with stable keys. Translate dynamic feedback explicitly with <s0></s0> and re-render graphics from existing state. Cover the complete enclosing page, including its title, metadata, navigation and documentation, and update the document language to match.
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0024: When source messages change, <s0></s0> identifies stale packs. Read the source diff, revise only affected messages, check their meaning, then set the new source fingerprint in each reconciled catalogue. <s1></s1> only prints the new fingerprint; it never silently marks translations as current. Keep coverage separate from independent review.
patterns-i18n-readme.msg0025: The first pattern has no rich-text renderer, localized search index, runtime translation service or localized no-JavaScript HTML. Add those only for an actual use case, using the same central requirement. Unsupported exact language tags fall back explicitly; this sample does not infer <s0></s0> from <s1></s1> automatically.
